(reference-curated-files)=

# Curated files

This page describes every file that people edit by hand under `curated/`.
The registers and lists are in `curated/mappings/`.
The community data is in `curated/community-contributions/`, and the PLIPs from before GitHub are in `curated/plips/`.

The format of a file is its Table Schema, in `curated/schemas/<kind>.json`.
`curated/datapackage.json` lists every file with its schema; `python -m scripts.tools.datapackage` writes it.
This page is generated from them with `python -m scripts.tools.schema_docs`, so edit the schema, not the page.
Run `python -m scripts.tools.check` or `make check` to validate the files.
It reports the file, the row and the column of every error.

A column that holds the ids of several rows of a register has several ids separated by semicolons.
Quote a value that contains a comma.
Save the files as UTF-8 with Unix line endings.
{doc}`/explanation/attribution` and {doc}`/explanation/curated-community-data` explain the rules behind the data.

## Registers

People, identities, affiliations, citations and organisations, in `curated/mappings/`.

### People

File: `curated/mappings/people.csv`

One row is one person.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | required; unique; pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$` | Opaque, stable identifier of the person: made once from the name when the row is created, and kept when the name changes. It is a key, not a spelling. |
| `name` | string | required | The name the person is published under. |

Primary key: `id`.

Checks beyond the schema:

- The rows are sorted by `id`.

### Identities

File: `curated/mappings/identities.csv`

One row is one string that denotes a person in the data: a GitHub login, a further GitHub account, a commit address or a spelling of the name, with the source that connects it to the person.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `person` | string | required; pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$`; id of a row of `people` | The id of the person in the people register. |
| `kind` | string | required; one of `github`, `github-alias`, `email`, `name`, `svn`, `irc`, `discourse` | The kind of identity: `github` the GitHub login the collected files count the person under (at most one per person), `github-alias` a further GitHub account, `email` a commit address, `name` a spelling of the name, `svn` a Subversion or CVS user, `irc` an IRC nick, `discourse` a handle on community.plone.org. |
| `value` | string | required | The login, address, spelling or handle as it appears in the data; a login with the case it has on GitHub. |
| `source` | string | pattern `^[0-9a-f]{12}$`; id of a row of `sources` | The id of the source in the source register that connects the person to the value. Required, except for an early commit address whose notes say what it rests on. |
| `snippet` | string |  | The words of the source that make the connection, verbatim from its excerpt; empty when no quote was verified. |
| `notes` | string |  | Free-text remarks: what the source shows, in our words, and other records. |

Primary key: `kind`, `value`.

Checks beyond the schema:

- An identity cites a source, unless it is an early commit address whose notes say what it rests on.
- A snippet appears in the excerpt of its source, compared as the capture compares a quote (`find_quote`).
- The rows are sorted by `person`, `kind`, `value`.
- `value` is unique within its `kind`, ignoring case.
- A person has at most one `github` identity, and a `github-alias` is nobody's `github`, ignoring case.

### Affiliations

File: `curated/mappings/affiliations.csv`

One row is one reading of the sources: one person, one organisation and one period, with its status.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | required; unique; pattern `^a[0-9a-f]{8}$` | Opaque, stable identifier of the affiliation: `a` and eight hex digits of a hash made once from person, organisation and years when the row is created, and kept when the row changes. The citations refer to it. |
| `person` | string | required; pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$`; id of a row of `people` | The id of the person in the people register. |
| `organisation` | string | required; pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$`; id of a row of `organisations` | The id of the organisation in the organisations register. |
| `from` | integer | required; at least 2000 | The first year the person belonged to the organisation. |
| `to` | integer | at least 2000 | The last year the person belonged to the organisation; empty while it lasts. |
| `status` | string | required; one of `stated`, `assumed`, `denied`, `proposed` | How the row reads its citations: `stated` they say so; `assumed` a range extended beyond its records, counted where no stated row covers the year; `denied` the person did not belong to the organisation in those years, which removes it from the counting; `proposed` a reading a tool produced and nobody has reviewed, never counted. |
| `checked` | date |  | The date the source was last checked. |
| `notes` | string |  | Free-text remarks on the row; for a denied row, the reason. |

Primary key: `id`.

Checks beyond the schema:

- `from` is not after `to`, and an affiliation without `to` says when its record was read.
- An assumed range stops at a record of another organisation that its own organisation returns after.
- The rows are sorted by `person`, `from`, `organisation`.
- Every affiliation but a proposal has at least one citation.
- No person-year is left undecided by the attribution rules: record a decision for each conflict.
- Of two decisions for one person and year, the later names the earlier in `supersedes`.

### Citations

File: `curated/mappings/citations.csv`

One row is one source that an affiliation rests on, with a passage of it; a source with several passages is cited once per passage.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `affiliation` | string | required; pattern `^a[0-9a-f]{8}$`; id of a row of `affiliations` | The id of the affiliation in the affiliations register. |
| `source` | string | required; pattern `^[0-9a-f]{12}$`; id of a row of `sources` | The id of the source in the source register that the affiliation rests on. |
| `snippet` | string |  | The words of the source that support the affiliation, verbatim from its excerpt; empty when no quote was verified. A source with several such passages is cited once per passage. |
| `supersedes` | string | ids of rows of `sources` separated by semicolons | For the citation of a decision: the ids of the earlier decisions that this one overrules. Several values are separated by semicolons. |
| `notes` | string |  | Free-text remarks: how the old data cited the source, and quotes not verified in its excerpt. |

Checks beyond the schema:

- A snippet appears in the excerpt of its source, compared as the capture compares a quote (`find_quote`).
- The rows are sorted by `affiliation`, `source`, `snippet`.
- `supersedes`: every element is the id of a row of the register, and none is repeated.

### Organisations

File: `curated/mappings/organisations.csv`

One row is one organisation.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | required; unique; pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$` | Opaque, stable identifier of the organisation: made once from the name when the row is created, and kept when the name changes. It is a key, not a spelling. |
| `name` | string | required; unique | The name the organisation is published under. |
| `kind` | string | required; one of `organisation`, `independent`, `foundation` | The kind of the organisation: a company, an independent or a foundation. |
| `github` | string | pattern `^[A-Za-z0-9](?:[A-Za-z0-9-]{0,37}[A-Za-z0-9])?$` | The login of the organisation's GitHub organisation, with the case it has on GitHub; empty when it has none. Commits in its repositories are evidence for an affiliation. |
| `aliases` | string |  | Other spellings of the name, separated by semicolons; free text, not keys. |
| `notes` | string |  | Free-text remarks on the row. |

Primary key: `id`.

Checks beyond the schema:

- The rows are sorted by `id`, ignoring case.
- No name or alias folds to the same text as the name or alias of another row.
- `github` is unique, ignoring case.

## Sources

The sources the registers cite, in `curated/sources/`, each with an excerpt file of the cited passages.

### Sources

File: `curated/sources/sources.csv`

One row is one source: a page, profile, commit, video or decision that we read once; its excerpt file holds the passages we cite.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | string | required; unique; pattern `^[0-9a-f]{12}$` | Opaque, stable identifier of the source: the first twelve hex digits of a hash of its normalised address and the archive timestamp. The normalised address keeps the fragment of a GitHub comment or review, which is a source of its own, and reduces a Google Doc to its document id. |
| `kind` | string | required; one of `page`, `speaker-page`, `profile`, `commit`, `video`, `pdf`, `register`, `issue-comment`, `decision` | What kind of source it is. |
| `title` | string | required | The title of the source as a reader sees it. |
| `date` | date | required | The date the source speaks for: its publication date if it shows one, else the capture date of the archived copy, else the day it was fetched. |
| `url` | string | required; pattern `^https?://.*$` | The address of the source on the web. |
| `archive_url` | string | pattern `^https://web\.archive\.org/web/\d{14}/https?://.*$` | The address of the Wayback Machine copy that was read, if one was. |
| `fetched` | datetime | required | When the source was read, in UTC. |
| `notes` | string |  | Anything a reader of the source needs to know. |

Primary key: `id`.

Checks beyond the schema:

- The id is the hash of the address and, for an archived copy, its timestamp.
- The rows are sorted by `id`.
- Every source has an excerpt file with a passage, and every excerpt file has a source.

## Lists

Accounts and repositories that the collectors treat in a special way, in `curated/mappings/`.

### Bot accounts

File: `curated/mappings/bot_accounts.csv`

One row is one GitHub account that is a bot.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `login` | string | required; unique | The GitHub login of the bot account. |
| `reason` | string | required | Why the account is counted as a bot. |

Primary key: `login`.

### Excluded repositories

File: `curated/mappings/excluded_repositories.csv`

One row is one repository of the `plone` organisation that the statistics skip.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `repository` | string | required; unique | The repository, as owner/name, left out of the statistics. |
| `reason` | string | required | Why the repository is left out. |

Primary key: `repository`.

## Community data

Community work per year and kind, in `curated/community-contributions/`.

### Board of Directors

File: `curated/community-contributions/YYYY-board-of-directors.csv`

One row is one member of the Board of Directors whose term ends in the year.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `person` | string | required; unique; pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$`; id of a row of `people` | The id of the person in the people register. |
| `role` | string | required; one of `voting`, `non-voting` | Whether the person is a voting or a non-voting member. |
| `source` | string | required; contains a web address | A public record, linked as a web address, that supports the row. |
| `notes` | string |  | Free-text remarks on the row. |

Primary key: `person`.

### Team leaders

File: `curated/community-contributions/YYYY-team-leaders.csv`

One row is one team leader and team.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `person` | string | required; pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$`; id of a row of `people` | The id of the person in the people register. |
| `team` | string | required | The team the person leads. |
| `source` | string | required; contains a web address | A public record, linked as a web address, that supports the row. |
| `notes` | string |  | Free-text remarks on the row. |

Primary key: `person`, `team`.

### Release managers

File: `curated/community-contributions/YYYY-release-managers.csv`

One row is one release manager.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `person` | string | required; unique; pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$`; id of a row of `people` | The id of the person in the people register. |
| `source` | string | required; contains a web address | A public record, linked as a web address, that supports the row. |
| `notes` | string |  | Free-text remarks on the row. |

Primary key: `person`.

### Podcasts

File: `curated/community-contributions/YYYY-podcasts.csv`

One row is one host of a Plone podcast or live series.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `series` | string | required | The podcast series. |
| `person` | string | pattern `^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9-]*$`; id of a row of `people` | The id of the host in the people register; empty when the source names no host. |
| `episodes` | integer | required; at least 1 | The number of episodes the person took part in. |
| `source` | string | required; contains a web address | A public record, linked as a web address, that supports the row. |
| `notes` | string |  | Free-text remarks on the row. |

### Plone Conference trainings

File: `curated/community-contributions/YYYY-plone-conference-trainings.csv`

One row is one training at the Plone Conference.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | required; unique | The title of the training. |
| `trainers` | string | ids of rows of `people` separated by semicolons | The ids of the trainers in the people register. Several values are separated by semicolons. |
| `source` | string | required; contains a web address | A public record, linked as a web address, that supports the row. |
| `notes` | string |  | Free-text remarks on the row. |

Primary key: `title`.

Checks beyond the schema:

- `trainers`: every element is the id of a row of the register, and none is repeated.

### World Plone Day talks

File: `curated/community-contributions/YYYY-world-plone-day-talks.csv`

One row is one video of a World Plone Day.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `title` | string | required | The title of the talk. |
| `speakers` | string | ids of rows of `people` separated by semicolons | The ids of the speakers in the people register. Several values are separated by semicolons. |
| `organisations` | string | ids of rows of `organisations` separated by semicolons | The ids of the organisations behind the talk in the organisations register. Several values are separated by semicolons. |
| `type` | string | required; one of `Talk`, `Teaser`, `Announcement`, `Welcome`, `Recap`, `Duplicate`, `Opening`, `Full stream`, `Newsroom` | The type of the recording. |
| `location` | string |  | Where the talk was given. |
| `source` | string | required; contains a web address | A public record, linked as a web address, that supports the row. |
| `notes` | string |  | Free-text remarks on the row. |

Checks beyond the schema:

- `speakers`: every element is the id of a row of the register, and none is repeated.
- `organisations`: every element is the id of a row of the register, and none is repeated.

### Conference talks

File: `curated/community-contributions/YYYY-conference-talks.csv`

One row is one keynote, talk or panel at a Plone conference, global or regional.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `event` | string | required | The conference, as it named itself, for example Plone Conference 2021 or Plone Tagung 2023. |
| `scope` | string | required; one of `global`, `regional` | `global` for the annual Plone Conference, `regional` for every other conference. |
| `type` | string | required; one of `Keynote`, `Talk`, `Panel` | Keynote, Talk or Panel, as the programme calls it; lightning-talk sessions are not recorded. |
| `title` | string | required | The title of the talk, as the programme gives it. |
| `speakers` | string | ids of rows of `people` separated by semicolons | The ids of the speakers in the people register. Several values are separated by semicolons. |
| `organisations` | string | ids of rows of `organisations` separated by semicolons | The ids of the organisations in the organisations register, for a talk that the programme attributes to a team instead of people. Several values are separated by semicolons. |
| `video` | string | pattern `^https?://.*$` | The web address of the recording, when one exists; one link, a second part goes to the notes. |
| `source` | string | required; contains a web address | A public record, linked as a web address, that supports the row: the programme or schedule page, the speaker page or the recording. |
| `notes` | string |  | Free-text remarks on the row. |

Checks beyond the schema:

- `speakers`: every element is the id of a row of the register, and none is repeated.
- `organisations`: every element is the id of a row of the register, and none is repeated.

### Sprints

File: `curated/community-contributions/YYYY-sprints.csv`

One row is one Plone sprint of the year.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sprint` | string | required; unique | The name of the sprint. |
| `start` | string | pattern `^\d{4}(-\d{2}(-\d{2})?)?$` | The first day of the sprint; the sources sometimes give only a year or a month. |
| `end` | string | pattern `^\d{4}(-\d{2}(-\d{2})?)?$` | The last day of the sprint, in the same form as the start. |
| `location` | string |  | Where the sprint took place. |
| `organisers` | string | ids of rows of `people` separated by semicolons | The ids of the organising persons in the people register. Several values are separated by semicolons. |
| `organisations` | string | ids of rows of `organisations` separated by semicolons | The ids of the organising organisations in the organisations register. Several values are separated by semicolons. |
| `level` | string | one of `strategic`, `community` | Whether the sprint was a strategic or a community sprint. |
| `source` | string | required; contains a web address | A public record, linked as a web address, that supports the row. |
| `notes` | string |  | Free-text remarks on the row. |

Primary key: `sprint`.

Checks beyond the schema:

- `organisers`: every element is the id of a row of the register, and none is repeated.
- `organisations`: every element is the id of a row of the register, and none is repeated.

## Recognition files and PLIPs

The recognition tables, see {doc}`recognition-files`, and the PLIPs from before GitHub.

### Community recognition levels

File: `curated/community-contributions/community-recognition-levels.csv`

One row is one recognition level.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Level` | string | required | The name of the recognition level. |
| `Min Points` | integer | required | The fewest points that reach the level. |
| `Max Points` | integer |  | The most points that still belong to the level; empty for the top level. |
| `Description` | string |  | A short description of the level. |

### Community recognition points

File: `curated/community-contributions/community-recognition-points.csv`

One row is one kind of contribution and its points.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Category` | string |  | The category of the contribution. |
| `Criteria` | string |  | The contribution that earns points. |
| `Comment` | string |  | How the points are split or limited. |
| `Period` | string |  | The period the points are counted for. |
| `Number of points` | integer |  | The points the contribution earns. |

### PLIPs before GitHub

File: `curated/plips/plone-plips-before-github.csv`

One row is one PLIP from before the PLIPs moved to GitHub issues, as the plone.org roadmap or a Trac ticket recorded it.

| Field | Type | Constraints | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Number` | string |  | The number of the PLIP in its numbering. |
| `Numbering` | string |  | The numbering the number belongs to, such as roadmap. |
| `Title` | string |  | The title of the PLIP. |
| `Proposer` | string |  | The proposer of the PLIP. |
| `Implementers` | string |  | The implementers of the PLIP. |
| `State` | string |  | The state of the PLIP. |
| `Proposed` | string |  | When the PLIP was proposed. |
| `Completed` | string |  | When the PLIP was completed. |
| `Release` | string |  | The Plone release that contains the PLIP. |
| `Same as` | string |  | The PLIP this one duplicates. |
| `Source` | string | required; contains a web address | A public record, linked as a web address, for the PLIP. |
| `Quote` | string |  | The words of the source that support the row. |
| `Notes` | string |  | Free-text remarks on the row. |
